assertionsTested.reason: On repeated fresh opens, the browser-rendered dashboard content was already visible in the first captured frame, so the app did not present an observable loading-only state before summary/goals/controls/table content appeared.
evidence: First frame at http://127.0.0.1:3100/index.html already showed goal cards, controls, and table rows instead of a loading-only surface.

assertionsTested.reason: Successful sheet fetch rendered the full dashboard in place on the same document with summary, goal cards, controls, result count, and grouped detail rows visible.
evidence: Browser URL remained http://127.0.0.1:3100/index.html after load.
Network observed GET https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bUY_Us-Vjq4JSYsnxrVXfAX6qRGjxZRgXR31me3Nc0U/gviz/tq?tqx=out:csv&gid=1636341361 during successful load.

assertionsTested.reason: Clicking refresh showed an in-progress state and then returned to the normal loaded dashboard without leaving duplicate error or loading UI behind.
evidence: Refresh was triggered from the in-page ↻ control and the URL stayed http://127.0.0.1:3100/index.html.
Network observed a second GET to the Google Sheets CSV endpoint after refresh.

assertionsTested.reason: When the sheet request was browser-intercepted and aborted, the page showed a dedicated error surface with a visible Try again action instead of a blank screen.
evidence: Failure was simulated by aborting the Google Sheets CSV request in-browser, then invoking refresh.
Error state remained at http://127.0.0.1:3100/index.html with visible Try again button.

assertionsTested.reason: After removing the abort route, activating Try again recovered from the error state back to the normal loaded dashboard in place.
evidence: Retry sequence: aborted sheet request -> error UI -> unroute intercept -> click Try again -> dashboard restored.

assertionsTested.reason: Initial load, simulated failure, retry recovery, and manual refresh all stayed on the same page URL with no path, hash, or query changes.
evidence: Observed URL at each stage: http://127.0.0.1:3100/index.html

assertionsTested.reason: Entering a non-matching search query produced an explicit no-results state while keeping the search box and reset controls visible so the user could understand and change the narrowing state.
evidence: Observed no-results message with search input still populated and controls still visible.

assertionsTested.reason: The zero-results state exposed a visible Reset narrowing recovery action and recovery restored the default loaded overview.
evidence: Recovery affordance shown: Reset narrowing button in the empty state; clicking it returned the full dashboard.

assertionsTested.reason: From first render onward the app behaved as a single in-place document with no routed shells or navigation transitions before interaction began.
evidence: No intermediate route, query, or hash changes occurred before interaction.

frictions.description: The live local page rendered loaded dashboard content too quickly to capture a loading-only frame, so VAL-LOAD-001 had to be judged from repeated first-frame screenshots rather than a clean isolated loading overlay capture. A separate zero-results recovery wait also used a text string that did not match the app's exact restored copy, so recovery was verified by direct snapshot/screenshot instead.

summary: Tested 9 browser load-basics assertions: 8 passed and 1 failed. The dashboard satisfied success, refresh, error/retry, URL stability, single-page, and zero-results recovery behaviors, but I could not observe a loading-only initial state before loaded content appeared.
